html:
Austria-Hungary, the Habsburg dual monarchy of Austria and Hungary, is shown here in 1914, the year it went to war. That war ended it four years later.

On 28 June 1914 a Bosnian Serb shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the throne, in Sarajevo. Vienna blamed Serbia, sent a harsh ultimatum, and declared war a month later. Alliances turned this into the First World War, with Germany on Austria's side and Russia, France and Britain against.

The army fared badly. It lost huge numbers to Russia in Galicia in 1914, needed German help to beat Serbia, and fought Italy along the Isonzo from 1915. Old Emperor Franz Joseph died in 1916. His successor, Charles I, tried to make a separate peace and failed. Hunger spread at home.

In October and November 1918 the empire broke apart as its peoples declared their own states: Czechoslovakia, the South Slav state that became Yugoslavia, a revived Poland, Austria and Hungary. The Treaty of Trianon and the treaty of Saint-Germain fixed the new borders.
